description: The symbolic neural network framework: building nets from layers with NetChain and NetGraph, encoders and decoders that convert real-world data to tensors, training with NetTrain, pretrained models from NetModel, and surgery, inspection and evaluation of nets.

tools.name: NetChain
tools.description: Builds a neural network as a linear chain of layers, inferring tensor shapes automatically between them. Layers can be named with an association for easier extraction later. It is the simplest way to define a feed-forward network.
tools.usage:
NetChain[{layer1, layer2, ...}]
NetChain[<|"name1" -> layer1, ...|>, "Input" -> spec, "Output" -> spec]
tools.notes: Use NetGraph when the topology branches, merges or has multiple inputs.

tools.name: NetGraph
tools.description: Builds a network with an arbitrary directed-acyclic-graph topology, allowing branches, skip connections and multiple inputs or outputs. Connectivity is specified as a list of rules between node names or indices. Use it for residual networks, siamese architectures and multi-task models.
tools.usage:
NetGraph[{layer1, layer2, ...}, {conn1, conn2, ...}]
NetGraph[<|"a" -> l1, "b" -> l2|>, {"a" -> "b"}]
tools.example:
net = NetGraph[
  <|"lin" -> LinearLayer[8], "act" -> ElementwiseLayer[Ramp],
    "sum" -> TotalLayer[]|>,
  {NetPort["Input"] -> "lin" -> "act", {"lin", "act"} -> "sum"},
  "Input" -> 4];
net[{1., 2., 3., 4.}]

tools.name: NetTrain
tools.description: Trains a network on data, handling batching, optimization, validation and progress reporting. Loss functions, optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes and target devices are all options. It returns the trained net, or a results object when asked.
tools.usage:
NetTrain[net, data]
NetTrain[net, data, All]
NetTrain[net, data, opts]

parameters.name: ValidationSet
parameters.description: Held-out data, or Scaled[f] to split off a fraction automatically.

parameters.name: MaxTrainingRounds
parameters.description: Number of passes over the data.

parameters.name: LossFunction
parameters.description: Explicit loss layer or port specification.

tools.notes: NetTrain[net, data, All] returns a NetTrainResultsObject with loss curves, timings and the best net found.

tools.name: NetTrainResultsObject
tools.description: Holds the full results of a training run, including the trained net, loss evolution, validation measurements, timings and the round at which the best net was found. It is returned by NetTrain when All is requested. Query it with property names like an association.

tools.name: NetModel
tools.description: Retrieves pretrained neural networks and model families from the Wolfram Neural Net Repository. Calling it with no arguments lists available models, and properties give architecture, size and task information. Use it for transfer learning and off-the-shelf inference.
tools.example:
net = NetModel["ResNet-50 Trained on ImageNet Competition Data"];
net[ExampleData[{"TestImage", "Mandrill"}]]
tools.notes: Models download on first use and can be large; NetModel["name", "UninitializedEvaluationNet"] gives the untrained architecture.

tools.name: NetEncoder
tools.description: Converts real-world data such as images, text, audio or class labels into the numeric tensors a network expects. It is attached to a net's input port and applied automatically on evaluation. Use it so that nets can accept raw objects directly.

tools.name: NetDecoder
tools.description: Converts the numeric output of a network back into meaningful objects such as class labels, probabilities, images or text. It attaches to the output port and is applied automatically. Use it to get interpretable results instead of raw tensors.

tools.name: LinearLayer
tools.description: Applies a fully connected affine transformation, multiplying the input by a weight matrix and adding a bias. Output size is given explicitly and input size is usually inferred. It is the fundamental parameterized layer of feed-forward networks.

tools.name: ConvolutionLayer
tools.description: Applies a convolution with a set of learned kernels, supporting stride, padding and dilation. It is the core layer of image and signal networks. Kernel size can be one-, two- or three-dimensional.
tools.usage:
ConvolutionLayer[n, s]
ConvolutionLayer[n, {h, w}, "Stride" -> s, "PaddingSize" -> p]

parameters.name: s
parameters.description: Kernel size, a number or list.

parameters.name: "Dilation"
parameters.description: Spacing between kernel elements for dilated convolutions.

tools.name: PoolingLayer
tools.description: Downsamples its input by taking the maximum, mean or total over sliding windows. It reduces spatial resolution and adds a degree of translation invariance. Window size, stride and function are configurable.

tools.name: BatchNormalizationLayer
tools.description: Normalizes activations across the batch and then applies a learned scale and shift. It stabilizes and accelerates training of deep networks. Behaviour differs between training and inference, which the framework handles automatically.
tools.notes: NormalizationLayer provides layer/instance/group normalization variants that do not depend on batch statistics.

tools.name: DropoutLayer
tools.description: Randomly zeroes a fraction of its inputs during training to reduce overfitting, and passes data through unchanged at inference time. The dropout probability is the main parameter. Use it between large fully connected layers.

tools.name: ElementwiseLayer
tools.description: Applies a scalar function independently to every element of its input, implementing activation functions. Named functions such as Ramp, Tanh, LogisticSigmoid and "ELU" are supported, as are custom expressions. Bare symbols like Ramp are automatically interpreted as this layer inside a NetChain.

tools.name: SoftmaxLayer
tools.description: Normalizes a vector of scores into a probability distribution that sums to one. It is the standard final layer for multi-class classification. A level specification selects which axis to normalize over.

tools.name: LongShortTermMemoryLayer
tools.description: Applies an LSTM recurrent layer to a sequence, maintaining a cell state and hidden state across time steps. It captures long-range dependencies better than a plain RNN. Use it for text, time series and any sequential data.

tools.name: GatedRecurrentLayer
tools.description: Applies a GRU recurrent layer, a simpler and faster alternative to LSTM with comparable accuracy on many tasks. It has fewer parameters because it merges the forget and input gates. Use it when training speed matters.

tools.name: AttentionLayer
tools.description: Computes attention between query, key and value sequences, the core operation of transformer architectures. Scoring function, multi-head splitting and masking are configurable. Use it for sequence-to-sequence models and self-attention blocks.

tools.name: EmbeddingLayer
tools.description: Maps integer token indices to dense learned vectors, the standard first layer of text networks. Vocabulary size and embedding dimension are specified. Pretrained embeddings can be supplied as initial weights.
tools.example:
net = NetChain[{EmbeddingLayer[16, 100], LongShortTermMemoryLayer[8],
  SequenceLastLayer[], LinearLayer[2], SoftmaxLayer[]},
  "Input" -> NetEncoder[{"Tokens", "English", "TargetLength" -> 20}]]

tools.name: CrossEntropyLossLayer
tools.description: Computes cross-entropy loss between predicted probabilities and targets, in index, probability or binary form. It is the standard loss for classification tasks. NetTrain attaches it automatically when the output decoder is a class decoder.

tools.name: MeanSquaredLossLayer
tools.description: Computes the mean squared difference between a network's output and a target, the standard regression loss. It is attached automatically when training a net with numeric outputs. Use MeanAbsoluteLossLayer when outliers should have less influence.

tools.name: NetInitialize
tools.description: Assigns initial values to all uninitialized learnable parameters of a net, using a chosen initialization method. Nets must be initialized before they can be evaluated outside of training. A random seed makes initialization reproducible.

tools.name: NetExtract
tools.description: Extracts a layer, sub-net, or a specific array such as weights or biases from a network. Paths are given as names, indices or nested lists. Use it to inspect parameters and to reuse parts of pretrained models.

tools.name: NetReplacePart
tools.description: Replaces layers, ports, encoders, decoders or arrays inside a net, returning a modified net. It is the main network-surgery operation, used for swapping heads or attaching encoders. The replacement must have compatible shapes.
tools.usage:
NetReplacePart[net, part -> new]
NetReplacePart[net, {"Output" -> dec, 3 -> layer}]

tools.name: NetTake
tools.description: Extracts a contiguous sub-network between two named or indexed layers, keeping the connections intact. It is the standard way to build a feature extractor from a pretrained classifier. The result is a usable net in its own right.
tools.notes: NetDrop removes layers instead of keeping them; NetFlatten expands nested chains first, which makes indices simpler.

tools.name: NetDrop
tools.description: Removes layers from the beginning or end of a chain, returning the remaining network. It is commonly used to strip a classification head before transfer learning. Layers may be given by name or index.

tools.name: NetFlatten
tools.description: Flattens nested NetChain and NetGraph structures into a single level, making layer paths simpler. It is useful before surgery on a pretrained model with deeply nested blocks. A level specification limits how far to flatten.

tools.name: NetPort
tools.description: Refers to a named input or output port of a network or layer, used when wiring NetGraph connections and when specifying losses. NetPort["Input"] and NetPort["Target"] are the most common. It also names ports of specific sub-layers.

tools.name: NetInformation
tools.description: Returns structural and statistical information about a network, such as the number of parameters, layer types, input and output shapes and a summary graphic. Property names select individual pieces of information. Use it to audit models before training or deployment.
tools.example:
net = NetModel["LeNet Trained on MNIST Data"];
NetInformation[net, "ArraysTotalElementCount"]

tools.name: NetMeasurements
tools.description: Evaluates a trained network on test data and reports metrics such as accuracy, loss, confusion matrices and per-class statistics. It is the neural-network counterpart of ClassifierMeasurements. Several measurements can be requested at once.

tools.name: NetMapOperator
tools.description: Applies a sub-network independently to each element of a sequence, sharing weights across positions. It is the neural equivalent of Map. Use it for per-token processing inside sequence models.
tools.notes: NetFoldOperator carries a state across the sequence, implementing custom recurrent cells.

tools.name: NetFoldOperator
tools.description: Runs a sub-network recurrently over a sequence, threading a state from one step to the next. It lets you define custom recurrent cells beyond the built-in LSTM and GRU layers. State ports are declared explicitly.

tools.name: NetArrayLayer
tools.description: Produces a learnable constant array as a network output, independent of any input. It is used for learned embeddings, positional encodings and trainable biases in custom architectures. The array shape is given explicitly.

tools.name: CatenateLayer
tools.description: Concatenates several input arrays along a specified dimension. It is the standard way to merge branches in a NetGraph. The non-concatenated dimensions must match.
tools.notes: ThreadingLayer combines inputs elementwise with a binary function; TotalLayer sums them.

tools.name: ThreadingLayer
tools.description: Combines several inputs elementwise using a given binary function, broadcasting shapes as needed. It implements residual additions, gating and elementwise products in NetGraph. Any listable function can be used.

tools.name: ReshapeLayer
tools.description: Reshapes its input to a specified tensor shape, with one dimension allowed to be inferred. It is needed when moving between convolutional and fully connected sections. FlattenLayer is the common special case.
tools.notes: FlattenLayer collapses all dimensions into one; TransposeLayer permutes them.

tools.name: NetExternalObject
tools.description: Represents a neural network defined outside the Wolfram Language, such as an imported ONNX or MXNet model. It can be converted into a native net or evaluated directly. Use it to bring models trained in other frameworks into Wolfram workflows.
tools.notes: Import with the "NetModel" element converts a supported external model into a native NetChain or NetGraph.
